tc.cite: Sherrington & Kirkpatrick, Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1792 (1975), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1792 (original, paywalled, not fetched); value read from Crisanti, Rizzo & Temesvari, Eur. Phys. J. B (2003), arXiv:cond-mat/0302538, Sec. 3 (expansions around H = 0 and T = Tc = 1, J = 1)
tc.independent_route: linearised RS equation: q = E tanh^2(beta sqrt(q) z) = beta^2 q + O(q^2), so q > 0 bifurcates at beta = 1; tests check q = 0 at beta = 0.9 and q > 0 at beta = 1.1 with replicant's own solver

rs_ground_energy.cite: Sherrington & Kirkpatrick, Phys. Rev. Lett. 35, 1792 (1975), doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.35.1792 (original, not fetched); value read from Stojnic, arXiv:2507.09247 (2025), Table 3, row '1 (full)' (RS): 0.79788, reported as -E0
rs_ground_energy.independent_route: closed form -sqrt(2/pi): T = 0 limit of e = -beta(1-q^2)/2 with beta(1-q) -> 2 phi(0) = E|z|; replicant computes -E|z| by quadrature and the test checks it against -sqrt(2/pi) to 1e-20

at_small_field_coefficient.cite: de Almeida & Thouless, J. Phys. A 11, 983 (1978), doi:10.1088/0305-4470/11/5/028 (original, paywalled, not fetched); coefficient read from Singh & Young, Phys. Rev. E 96, 012127 (2017), arXiv:1705.01164, Fig. 3 (asymptotic SK AT line h = (4/3)^(1/2) (Tc - T)^(3/2), J = Tc = 1). Meaning: h_AT^2 = c (1 - T)^3 + ... as h -> 0
at_small_field_coefficient.independent_route: replicant's own AT line: root in beta of the replicon 1 - beta^2 E sech^4(beta(h + sqrt(q) z)) at h = 0.01, 0.02, 0.04, ratio h^2/(1-T)^3 extrapolated to 1-T = 0 (slow test). The value 4/3 is exact; tol measures the quality of our 3-point extrapolation (it gives 1.33191), not disagreement between sources

rsb1_ground_energy.cite: Stojnic, arXiv:2507.09247 (2025), Table 3: level-2 fully-lifted RDT row '2 (full)' (q2 = 0.4768, q1 -> 1): 0.76526, reported as -E0; identified with 1RSB with free q0 (identification confirmed by our own solve: q0 = 0.47678, E = -0.7652594). Original 1RSB: Parisi, J. Phys. A 13, L115 (1980), doi:10.1088/0305-4470/13/4/009 (not fetched: publisher blocked the download)
rsb1_ground_energy.independent_route: replicant's own T = 0 1RSB solve: stationary point in (q0, mu = beta m) of E(q0, mu) = mu(1-q0^2)/4 - (1/mu) E_z ln E_y exp(mu |sqrt(q0) z + sqrt(1-q0) y|), derived here from the finite-T 1RSB functional (q1 -> 1, m -> 0 at fixed beta m); does not use the paper's number

rsb2_ground_energy.cite: Stojnic, arXiv:2507.09247 (2025), Table 3 ('rr-sfl RDT parameters; CLUP SK model; rx=1', c1 -> 1, n, beta -> oo): row '3 (full)' (q = 0.3215, 0.8496, q -> 1): 0.76361, reported as -E0; identified with 2RSB (two free overlaps below q = 1), the identification confirmed by our own solve (q = 0.32140, 0.84950)
rsb2_ground_energy.independent_route: replicant's own T = 0 2-step Parisi staircase (families/parisi.py krsb_ground_energy(2)): maximum over (q0, q1, mu1, mu2) of the K-step functional, Newton on the adjoint gradient; does not use the paper's number. tol 1e-5 = the table's last digit

rsb3_ground_energy.cite: Stojnic, arXiv:2507.09247 (2025), Table 3 ('rr-sfl RDT parameters; CLUP SK model; rx=1', c1 -> 1, n, beta -> oo): row '4 (full)' (q = 0.2462, 0.7031, 0.9410, q -> 1): 0.76331, reported as -E0; identified with 3RSB
rsb3_ground_energy.independent_route: replicant's own T = 0 3-step Parisi staircase (families/parisi.py krsb_ground_energy(3)); does not use the paper's number. Our point has E = -0.7633135 and q = (0.2439, 0.6989, 0.9396): the energy agrees to the table's digits, the overlaps only to ~4e-3 (the functional is flat along those directions: Hessian eigenvalues down to -2e-5), so only the energy is banked. tol 1e-5 = the table's last digit

fullrsb_ground_energy.cite: Oppermann, Schmidt & Sherrington, Phys. Rev. Lett. 98, 127201 (2007), arXiv:cond-mat/0608581: E_inf = -0.7631667265(6) (k-RSB extrapolation); same digits in Schmidt & Oppermann, arXiv:0801.1756 (2008): -0.763166726566547
fullrsb_ground_energy.independent_route: replicant's own Parisi solve (families/parisi.py): T = 0 K-step staircases K = 1..8 maximised over (q, mu), audited (gradient, Hessian, grid refinement), extrapolated in K with a fitted power law E_K = E_inf - C K^-s from K = 6, 7, 8; error estimate = the whole extrapolated tail (6.9e-6) plus grid and optimiser terms. Does not use the banked number (it is the test's target). tol 2e-4 covers the spread of the sources below (largest gap 1.33e-4, Parisi 1980); two independent published methods agree to 5e-5 (Crisanti-Rizzo infinite-RSB PDE vs Oppermann et al. high-order k-RSB)
